papers.title: Can We Defend Against AI-Generated Video Attacks on Real-World Crisis Events? A Systematic Evaluation of Detectors, Generators and Social Dissemination

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced RA-Bench, a benchmark of 17,886 videos across 10 social-risk categories, revealing that current AI video detectors fail to generalize and degrade further during social dissemination.
key_points: RA-Bench pairs 1,830 real-video anchors with 16,056 synthetic clips generated by 4 open-source and 5 closed-source models across 10 social-risk categories.
Evaluated 19 detection systems—7 traditional detectors, 10 zero-shot multimodal models under 3 review settings, and 2 fine-tuned MLLMs—finding none generalized consistently across RA-Bench instances.
Detectability varies by generation quality and conditioning, while source-level detection patterns remain stable across sampling seeds.
Human authenticity tests show that synthetic videos capable of fooling human perception are similarly difficult for automated detectors to classify correctly.
Simulated social dissemination degrades overall detector reliability, exacerbating real-world failure rates.
summary.why_it_matters: Existing deepfake detection pipelines are unreliable for real-world crisis management because they fail to generalize to modern video generators and degrade under social media sharing conditions.

papers.title: Beyond Final Scores: A Systematic Evaluation of Agents for Long-Horizon AI Research and Development

summary.tldr: A new evaluation framework uses rule-based metrics and controlled comparisons across 36 long-horizon tasks to analyze seven frontier agents' internal behaviors, experience reuse, and execution bottlenecks beyond final scores.
key_points: Evaluates seven frontier models across 36 long-horizon AI R&D tasks by analyzing Solution Framing, Execution, and Feedback Control.
Finds agents function as engineering optimizers that adapt or combine established techniques rather than generating genuine methodological novelty.
Shows performance is heavily influenced by high run-to-run variance, experience reuse that can either aid or mislead decisions, and evaluation harness design.
Identifies that similar final performance scores often mask vastly different process-level bottlenecks.
summary.why_it_matters: Evaluating internal agent behaviors and experience reuse rather than relying on static end-state scores provides actionable insights for improving LLM training, inference-time strategies, and harness design.

papers.title: Intern-S2-Mobius: Foundation Model with Decoupled Knowledge and Reasoning

summary.tldr: Intern-S2-Mobius introduces Mobius-v0, an architecture that decouples knowledge storage from reasoning by utilizing a globally shared feed-forward network memory and multiple self-attention reasoners.
key_points: Reasoners query a globally shared Feed-Forward Network (FFN) memory for knowledge vectors while using hidden states as a cache and carrier.
A 7B model trained from scratch matches a 7B Transformer baseline's downstream score using only 62.6% of the training data.
Intern-S2-Mobius, continually pretrained from Qwen3.5-35B, maintains baseline downstream performance while providing nearly 4x end-to-end inference speedup.
summary.why_it_matters: Decoupling knowledge from reasoning significantly reduces training data requirements and dramatically improves model inference efficiency without sacrificing downstream task performance.

papers.title: MobileMem: Learning from a Year of Mobile Experiences

summary.tldr: MobileMem is a new benchmark and framework for on-device long-term memory, built on a year-scale collection of mobile experiences to evaluate continuous, multimodal agent learning.
key_points: Uses a knowledge-grounded synthesis pipeline to generate coherent, temporally consistent trajectories from user-app sessions.
Covers both text and multimodal settings across extended time horizons.
Evaluates multi-hop reasoning, temporal reasoning, dynamic knowledge updating, and implicit preference inference.
Focuses on modeling continuous user experiences rather than isolated, static factual retrieval.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables the evaluation and development of persistent personal AI assistants that can adapt to changing user preferences and context over long periods on mobile devices.

papers.title: HumanTracker: Towards Comprehensive and Human-Aligned Motion Tracking Benchmark

summary.tldr: HumanTracker is a humanoid motion tracking benchmark providing 153 hours of optical motion trajectories and HumanScore, a preference-aligned metric trained on 12K motion pairs to detect stability and contact failures.
key_points: Addresses limitations of traditional kinematic metrics, which average per-frame pose errors but miss physical artifacts like foot skating, mistimed touch-downs, and unstable support.
Provides a dataset containing approximately 153 hours of optical motion trajectories across four motion families with text labels.
Introduces HumanScore, a evaluation metric trained on 12K motion pairs (24K total motions) that aligns with human preference.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables more accurate evaluation of humanoid tracking algorithms by capturing contact-rich, long-horizon physical instabilities that standard kinematic metrics overlook.

papers.title: CPI-Bench: A Comprehensive,Practical and Intelligent Benchmark for Real-World Image Editing

summary.tldr: CPI-Bench is a new benchmark for evaluating real-world image editing models across multi-image inputs, practical user scenarios, and complex reasoning-based instructions.
key_points: CPI-General-Bench evaluates diverse single and multi-image editing tasks.
CPI-Practical-Bench assesses model performance on high-frequency real-user application scenarios.
CPI-Intelligent-Bench focuses on challenging, reasoning-based editing instructions.
Ranking analysis shows CPI-Bench achieves the highest alignment with the human-preference Arena Image Edit Leaderboard.
summary.why_it_matters: CPI-Bench provides a human-aligned, reliable standard to quantify model gaps in real-world deployment and complex multi-image reasoning tasks.

papers.title: Claim-Level Reliability Assessment for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning

summary.tldr: Claim-Level Reliability Assessment (CLR) is a training-free framework that improves test-time reasoning by decomposing traces into critical claims and using semantic falsification to target errors.
key_points: Reallocates compute from solution sampling to verification by extracting decision-critical claims from reasoning traces to avoid signal dilution.
Leverages semantic falsification asymmetry, focusing compute on identifying a single decisive flaw in a claim rather than generating a complete, flawless solution.
Applies nonlinear reliability scoring to compress the survival space of high-confidence incorrect traces and reduce erroneous consensus.
Achieved a 27.15 percentage-point increase over pass@1 on GPT-OSS-20B/CMIMC25, while raising self-consistency accuracy from 77.50% to 82.19% using 37.0% fewer tokens.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables large language models to achieve higher reasoning accuracy with reduced token consumption during test-time compute allocation.

papers.title: Forecast Collapse in Time-Series Foundation Models

summary.tldr: Researchers identified forecast collapse in time-series foundation models on low-predictability targets and introduced CalibRank, an objective function that balances forecast calibration and cross-sectional ranking accuracy.
key_points: Forecast collapse causes point predictions to become nearly flat and ruins cross-sectional ranking performance when target predictability is low, such as in hourly stock returns.

Per-series loss functions like squared error force low-amplitude forecasts to maintain calibration, whereas cross-sectional correlation objectives improve ranking but inflate prediction amplitude by over 10x.
CalibRank balances calibration and ranking loss, nearly tripling cross-sectional correlation on the Finance1K benchmark while maintaining target-level forecast amplitude across tested models.
summary.why_it_matters: Standard per-series evaluation metrics obscure cross-series structural failures, which can render foundation model forecasts unusable for downstream multi-asset decision-making.

papers.title: PRM-as-a-Judge 1.5: A Toolkit for Robot Process Assessment

summary.tldr: PRM-as-a-Judge 1.5 is a robot process assessment toolkit that converts rollout videos into dense progress curves to measure failure-side progress, post-drawdown recovery, and execution quality beyond binary success rates.
key_points: Introduces three new metrics building on version 1.0 to evaluate failure-side progress, post-drawdown recovery, and success-side execution quality.
Converts robot rollout videos into dense progress curves to extract fine-grained process scores.
Includes RoboPulse++, an updated evaluation framework designed to test the reliability of process reward models (PRMs).
Releases a suite containing benchmarks, metric implementations, and visualization tools for reproducible manipulation evaluation.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables fine-grained, transparent, and reproducible evaluation of embodied AI models beyond simple binary success metrics.

papers.title: Marionette: Predicting World States, Rendering Geometry, Painting Appearance

summary.tldr: Marionette introduces a game world model that decouples dynamics from rendering by predicting explicit 3D world states, converting them to pose-control videos via a zero-parameter graphics engine, and synthesizing RGB frames using a video-diffusion model.
key_points: Predicts a 276-dimensional explicit 3D world state tracking multi-entity articulated skeletons, metric root trajectories, and rotations using a two-stage autoregressive model.
Uses a zero-parameter graphics bridge to compute world-space geometry and occlusion in closed form, outputting structured pose-control videos to condition a diffusion observation model.
Enables state-level programmatic corrections: applying a terrain collider and separation cap reduced ground penetration by 66% and prevented character drift without retraining the observation model.
Achieves visual fidelity comparable to recorded pose controls, scoring an FVD of 831 for generated states versus 799 for ground-truth recorded states.
summary.why_it_matters: Decoupling explicit world-state dynamics from appearance rendering eliminates compound error accumulation in long-horizon game simulations and allows direct programmatic control over physics and character interactions.

papers.title: Latent On-Policy Self-Distillation

summary.tldr: Latent On-Policy Self-Distillation (LOPD) makes the teacher's privileged context learnable end-to-end via continuous latent tokens rather than relying on designer-specified artifacts like answers, skills, or feedback.
key_points: LOPD retrieves past experiences and composes them into continuous latent tokens that condition a self-teacher.
The student policy generates trajectories from task and interaction history, receiving dense token-level supervision at every visited prefix.
A privileged-margin objective is introduced to regulate and stabilize the learning of the latent context.
LOPD outperforms RLVR, OPSD, SDPO, and Skill-SD on agentic tool use and code generation while using under 30% of the rollout budget required by GRPO and Skill-SD.
summary.why_it_matters: By eliminating human-engineered privileged context, LOPD enables more scalable, sample-efficient, and end-to-end self-improvement for autonomous agents.

papers.title: Second Thought: Reasoning in Parallel as LLM Agents Act and Observe

summary.tldr: Second Thought is a training-free inference framework that runs parallel auxiliary reasoning branches during the action-observation idle window of LLM agents to reduce main-thread sequential decoding without sacrificing task accuracy.
key_points: Identifies the interval when an agent executes an action and awaits environment observation as a reasoning idle window.
Forks four auxiliary branches immediately after the main Thought phase concludes, decodes them concurrently, and merges the resulting thoughts upon receiving the environment observation.
Reduces main-thread decoding by up to 43% (averaging ~20% across six settings) and lowers the average turn count across all nine evaluated model-benchmark pairs.
Maintains or improves Pass@1 accuracy, yielding significant performance increases of +12.4 and +10.2 points in two evaluation settings.
Outperforms a compute-matched control that forces equivalent reasoning budget onto the main thread, achieving higher Pass@1 with 1.3 to 3.2 fewer sequential decoding steps.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables LLM agents to perform deeper reasoning without increasing main-thread latency, accelerating agent execution times while maintaining or improving benchmark success rates.

papers.title: Scaling Domain Data Repetition in LLM Pretraining

summary.tldr: A study on scaling domain data repetition shows that optimal repetition counts mildly increase with model size at a fixed tokens-per-parameter ratio and correlate negatively with a domain's final validation loss.
key_points: At a fixed tokens-per-parameter (TPP) ratio, the optimal repetition count for high-quality domain data mildly increases as the model size scales.
Optimal repetition count strongly correlates negatively with the domain's final validation loss, meaning lower-loss domains tolerate and benefit from higher repetition.
The total volume of unique domain data shows only a weak relationship to its optimal repetition count.
Optimal repetition counts tuned on smaller proxy models with identical TPP ratios can serve as practical estimates for larger LLMs.
summary.why_it_matters: Practitioners can safely reuse high-quality data repetition schedules optimized on smaller proxy models to prevent domain dilution in larger models without causing severe overfitting.

papers.title: LittleLearner: Language Models Under Pedagogically Controlled Knowledge Exposure

summary.tldr: Researchers introduced LITTLECURRICULUM, an 88B-token elementary-level corpus, and LITTLELEARNER, a 5B-parameter model trained on it to establish controlled, interpretable knowledge boundaries for studying LLM capability acquisition.
key_points: LITTLECURRICULUM is an 88B-token pretraining dataset strictly capped at U.S. Grade 5 concepts, facts, and vocabulary.
LITTLELEARNER is a 5B-parameter language model trained from scratch on LITTLECURRICULUM to act as a developmentally restricted sandbox.
Post-training and in-context learning experiments demonstrated that injecting new knowledge helps the model better utilize existing capabilities without raising out-of-scope abilities.
summary.why_it_matters: This controlled sandbox allows researchers to study how language models acquire, represent, and use knowledge without the confounding effects of heterogeneous, web-scale pretraining data.

papers.title: UniProbe: A Learnable Token-Level Hallucination Detector for Large VLMs using Multi-Structural Internal Representations

summary.tldr: UniProbe is a learnable token-level hallucination detector that models a frozen LVLM's computational trace using interleaved GNN, ViT, and GRU modules over a directed graph of attention weights.
key_points: Models the computational trace from a single forward pass as a directed graph over image patches, query tokens, and generated tokens using attention weights.
Processes structural evidence by interleaving a GNN for relational structure, a ViT for 2-D visual geometry, and a GRU for sequential response order.
Includes a streaming variant for hallucination-aware decoding via online resampling and a self-adaptation strategy to align with the base model's generations.
Reduces object hallucinations by up to 55% during decoding with 1.06x standard generation latency without requiring full-model fine-tuning.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables real-time, low-latency mitigation of vision-language hallucinations at the token level without requiring computationally expensive full-model retraining or external verifiers.

papers.title: Handover of In-Context Learning State Across Session Boundaries

summary.tldr: This study establishes a theoretical framework for session handover in large language models by framing context transfer as preserving task-relative in-context learning states under strict memory constraints.
key_points: Defines predictive equivalence under an exogeneity condition as the coarsest deterministic sufficient handover, establishing a fixed-length bit requirement.
Proposes a three-part record structure combining exact decisions and constraints, task-justified statistics for repeated evidence, and essential unrepresented raw observations.
Derives exact finite-dimensional handovers for Gaussian linear regression alongside finite-bit perturbation bounds and nonparametric prediction error bounds.
summary.why_it_matters: It provides a mathematically grounded methodology for determining exactly what context to compress or retain when switching sessions, agents, or memory windows without sacrificing downstream predictive performance.

papers.title: SimpleOPD: Simple Tokenizer-Agnostic On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning

summary.tldr: SimpleOPD enables tokenizer-agnostic on-policy distillation from long-context teacher models to short-context students by aligning text-span tokens and using constrained KL loss to stabilize generation length.
key_points: Aligns student and teacher tokens in a shared text space by targeting only identical text spans to solve tokenizer mismatch.
Mitigates teacher-student distribution mismatch and response length explosion using a student reference KL loss.
Masks advantages of special termination tokens like <|im_end|> and <|endoftext|> to prevent unstable truncation and manage steady length growth.
Demonstrates performance gains across student families (Qwen3, Qwen3.5, Intern-S2, GLM-4.7, Gemma-4) using the SU-01 teacher model.
Intern-S2-Preview gained 21.2 points on ProofBench (reaching 55.2) and showed cross-domain gains on HLE and HiPhO science benchmarks.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables smaller, short-context models to efficiently absorb advanced proof-reasoning capabilities from long-context teacher models without requiring identical tokenizers or risking training instability.

papers.title: Approximate Muon with low-rank adapters

summary.tldr: sMuon adapts the Muon optimizer for low-rank fine-tuning by approximating a relaxed objective through linearization and least-squares, enabling low-rank updates using only matrix multiplication operations.
key_points: Addresses the mathematical impossibility of orthogonalizing low-rank weight updates in standard LoRA.
Formulates sMuon (small Muon) by approximating a relaxed Muon objective via linearization followed by a least-squares step.
Provides an efficient implementation relying solely on matrix multiplication (matmul) operations rather than complex linear algebra decompositions.
Demonstrates performance improvements in supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and ReLoRA pretraining experiments.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods like LoRA to leverage the optimization benefits of Muon using computationally efficient matrix multiplications.

papers.title: Designing Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Models: A Unified Path-Space View

summary.tldr: This paper unifies reverse-trajectory and forward-matching diffusion RL methods under a single path-space policy-gradient framework, revealing that empirical performance gaps stem from variance reduction rather than differing algorithmic principles.
key_points: Derives a path-space policy-gradient estimator using importance sampling between SDEs, proving Flow-GRPO's Itô integral formulation is equivalent to the forward-matching structure in AWM and DiffusionNFT via a value-gradient transformation.
Identifies a unified design space organized by value-gradient estimation, weight functions, and trajectory sampling choices.
Introduces a multi-sample KDE value-gradient estimator that reuses rollout groups alongside scale-bounded weight families to prevent singular weight instabilities.
Validates the framework experimentally on SD3.5-M and Qwen-Image models, demonstrating improvements over existing diffusion-RL baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It clarifies the mathematical connection between fragmented diffusion-RL algorithms, allowing practitioners to systematically design more stable, variance-reduced post-training recipes for image diffusion models.

papers.title: More Correct Mass, Worse Answers: Why Power Sampling Can Fail and How to Fix It

summary.tldr: Researchers identified critical mismatches in inference-time Power Sampling that degrade downstream performance and proposed a deformation-controlled, support-preserving target to fix them.
key_points: Uncovered a paradox where Power Sampling increases probability mass on correct trajectories but causes accuracy drops up to 18.5 percentage points in self-consistency evaluation.
Identified dose mismatch, where a fixed exponent creates inconsistent distributional changes across different problems.
Identified coverage mismatch, where global sharpening concentrates probability mass on narrow paths and destroys the broad trajectory diversity required for downstream aggregation.
Replaced uniform trajectory exponentiation with a calibrated, support-preserving Power target that limits the suppression of moderate-probability paths.
Demonstrated that combining the repaired sampler with weighted self-consistency reverses performance losses and outperforms standard multi-sample inference under the same budget.
summary.why_it_matters: Fixing Power Sampling enables verifier-free inference-time reasoning techniques to improve accuracy without accidentally destroying the trajectory diversity needed for search and aggregation.

papers.title: Local and Global Regimes of Geometric Complexity in Language Model Representations

summary.tldr: Researchers identified two scale-dependent intrinsic dimensionality (ID) regimes in language model representations driven by dataset lexical diversity and derived an exact, parameter-free formula predicting the exact reversal point between them.
key_points: At low lexical diversity, datasets with fewer unique last-token items yield higher ID estimates.
At high lexical diversity, the trend reverses and datasets with more unique final words yield higher ID estimates.
The authors derived an exact, parameter-free formula for the transition point that matches empirical observations across all tested scales.
The findings demonstrate that ID estimates reflect dataset construction properties, specifically final-token lexical diversity, rather than purely intrinsic model or linguistic complexity.
summary.why_it_matters: Practitioners cannot treat intrinsic dimensionality as a simple proxy for representation complexity without accounting for dataset lexical diversity and scale dependencies.

papers.title: Amplified Does Not Mean Predictive: Reasoning Behaviors in Thinking Models

summary.tldr: A study introducing Behavioral Lift across 15 models and 15,282 traces reveals an Amplification-Lift Gap, where reasoning-oriented training amplifies behaviors like uncertainty acknowledgment without increasing high-correctness behaviors like confidence calibration.
key_points: Introduces Behavioral Lift to quantify how much correctness changes when a specific reasoning behavior is present versus absent in model traces.
Evaluated 15 models across 6 text-only and vision-language benchmarks, analyzing a taxonomy of core behaviors in 15,282 annotated traces.
Identifies an Amplification-Lift Gap: thinking models amplify uncertainty acknowledgment by 3-7x despite its weak or negative association with correctness.
High-lift behaviors strongest for correctness—such as confidence calibration, knowledge alignment, and self-awareness—are barely amplified by current reasoning training.
summary.why_it_matters: Reasoning training optimizes surface-level deliberative traces rather than predictive correctness, highlighting the need for process-level objectives that reward grounded and calibrated reasoning.

papers.title: Split the Labor: Separating Evidence Interpretation from Decision Aggregation

summary.tldr: A framework that separates LLM evidence interpretation from decision aggregation using a four-field evidence tuple, correcting count-scale drift by pooling calibrated log-likelihood ratios instead of raw score summation.
key_points: Defines a structured four-field evidence tuple consisting of hypothesis, reliability bucket, rationale, and provenance to decouple source reading from decision logic.
Identifies count-scale drift, where thresholding unnormalized source weight sums causes the operating point to slide as the number of consulted sources increases or reader reliability improves.
Demonstrates that pooling calibrated log-likelihood ratios mathematically aligns vote rules with posterior ordering when source reliabilities vary.
Combines a small sequence encoder trained on an auxiliary objective with a tree ensemble under censored survival loss, increasing AUPRC from 0.805 to 0.921 on a longitudinal corpus.
summary.why_it_matters: Fixing the arithmetic of multi-source evidence aggregation prevents systematic calibration drift without requiring larger language models or complex architectural changes.

papers.title: Twin: Playing an Unknown Game with a Test-Time Digital Twin

summary.tldr: Twin uses a frontier coding agent to generate and iteratively repair executable world models at test-time for zero-shot grid games, achieving a 93.3% score on the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark.
key_points: Twin constructs world models by converting transition prediction mismatches into code counterexamples to repair the executable program.
A replay validation harness prevents game actions until the generated model perfectly reproduces all previously observed game transitions.
Twin cleared 179 out of 183 levels (97.8%), outperforming human efficiency on 88.3% of cleared levels.
The system inferred the underlying goal prior to receiving any reward signal in 87.2% of cleared levels, using search to discover goals for the rest.
Twin raised the base model benchmark score from 7.8% (and 61.1% with an off-the-shelf harness) to 93.3%, clearing 23 of 25 full games.
summary.why_it_matters: This approach demonstrates that frontier LLMs can automatically reverse-engineer executable environment dynamics and unseen goals purely through test-time interaction and code refinement.

papers.title: Knowing When to Stop: Bayesian Optimal Stopping for LLM Evaluations

summary.tldr: The optstop framework uses precision-based Bayesian adaptive stopping to dynamically allocate LLM evaluation compute based on uncertainty rather than fixed sampling budgets.
key_points: Employs hierarchical Bayesian inference across binary, ordinal, and continuous outcomes without needing a calibrated item bank.
Keeps every benchmark item eligible for sampling while halting evaluation once estimates achieve sufficient precision or stability.
Includes a low-performance safeguard that increases sampling caution as performance approaches zero to accurately capture rare successes.
Achieved 57% to 97% reductions in planned evaluation trials across nine validation settings in a 200-item, 10-epoch test without altering conclusions.
summary.why_it_matters: It significantly reduces compute costs and runtime for LLM benchmarking without sacrificing statistical confidence or accuracy in the final results.

summary.tldr: A new attack technique demonstrated in recent research allows the recovery of encrypted, base64-encoded LLM reasoning traces sent via proprietary messaging protocols.
key_points: AI labs like OpenAI and Anthropic include encrypted reasoning traces inside base64-encoded blobs within their messaging protocols.
A paper titled 'Stealing Reasoning Traces from Proprietary LLM APIs' details an elegant technique to decrypt and recover these hidden reasoning traces.
summary.why_it_matters: This vulnerability allows attackers to extract proprietary internal reasoning traces from AI models even when transmitted as encrypted payloads.

security.title: Finding Vulnerabilities via LLM-Augmented Semantics-Aware Type-Checking

summary.tldr: SETYPE uses Large Language Models to derive type systems from code variable/function semantics, converting vulnerability detection into a semantics-aware type-checking process.
key_points: SETYPE derives a semantics-aware type system directly from source code based on the natural language meanings of symbols and expressions.
Type inference and type checking are offloaded entirely to LLMs, where a failed type check signals a potential security vulnerability.
PYSETYPE, a Python web application prototype, achieved 87% detection precision and 88% detection accuracy in real-world evaluations.
The tool identified 15 potential zero-day vulnerabilities, with nine officially confirmed by developers.
summary.why_it_matters: It replaces manual syntactic rule-writing in static analysis by leveraging LLM semantic understanding to automate complex zero-day vulnerability discovery.

security.title: MazeRunner: Nonlinear Task and Clue Orchestration for LLM-driven Black-Box Automated Penetration Testing

summary.tldr: MazeRunner is an autonomous penetration testing system that uses a three-agent framework to handle nonlinear attack paths, task states, and long-range clue correlation in black-box environments.
key_points: Architecture decouples global orchestration, context-intensive execution, and failure-oriented review while maintaining persistent task states and evidence.
Enables nonlinear testing operations including action revision, prerequisite recovery, dynamic branch switching, and cross-horizon clue correlation.
Evaluated on 10 Hack The Box (HTB) targets under a strict 20 million LLM token limit per run without target-specific leakage.
Achieved a 47.7% subtask completion rate using Claude Sonnet 4.5, outperforming PentestGPT-V2 (36.2%) and Claude Code (34.2%).
Gained user-level access on six targets and root access on two, whereas same-model baselines reached user access on only two targets and never achieved root.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that decoupling task orchestration from execution enables LLM agents to navigate complex, nonlinear black-box networks and escalate privileges without getting trapped in linear depth-first paths.

security.title: P2Skill: Privacy Preserving Skill Distillation for Cloud-Local LLM Inference Systems

summary.tldr: P2Skill uses prompt-based skill distillation to enable local small language models to handle PII-aware routing, paraphrasing, and reconstruction without requiring model fine-tuning or learned auxiliary detectors.
key_points: Local SLMs perform decomposition, PII-aware routing, paraphrasing, and reconstruction via skill prompts without privacy-specific fine-tuning.
Skills are iteratively refined by a cloud LLM using execution failures, improving generalization beyond memorized PII patterns.
Evaluations across a four-domain benchmark demonstrate a 1.69x to 3.66x improvement in privacy-preserved inference quality over existing baselines.
summary.why_it_matters: It enables accurate cloud-local LLM inference while protecting sensitive user data on personal devices without the computational overhead of model re-training.

security.title: Regime-Conditional Verification: Correctness Estimation for Adapting and Monitoring Safety Classifiers

summary.tldr: Regime-Conditional Verification (RCV) is a lightweight wrapper that uses a classifier's internal representations to estimate policy disagreement, correct false predictions, and detect distribution shift without retraining the underlying model.
key_points: RCV estimates the probability of prediction disagreement with a deployer's target policy using internal representations from off-the-shelf safety classifiers.
It selectively corrects predictions likely to be wrong, catching up to 0.81 of previously missed unsafe content across tested datasets without modifying the classifier.
Label-free correctness estimates enable shift detection, triggering a maintenance loop that updates the RCV layer and reserves full classifier fine-tuning for unresolved drift episodes.
In a deployment study with ten held-out attack campaigns, RCV detected every campaign in a dedicated injection panel and repaired most drift episodes without classifier fine-tuning.
summary.why_it_matters: RCV enables dynamic adaptation and real-time drift monitoring for safety classifiers without the high computational cost of frequent model fine-tuning.

security.title: Does Fixing Break Security? An Empirical Study of Security Degradation in Iterative LLM-Driven Infrastructure-as-Code Repair

summary.tldr: A study of LLM-driven Infrastructure-as-Code repair reveals that iterative fixes cause true security regressions in 3.3% of scenarios, primarily driven by resource restructuring and high code churn.
key_points: Analysis of 5,968 IaC-Eval scenario timelines across 15 configurations identified true security regressions (strict detection) in 3.3% of scenarios and 5.2% of iteration transitions.
Resource restructuring accounted for 79.0% of root causes, with regression transitions exhibiting 2.6x more code churn (Cohen's d=0.90) and 4.9x higher check volatility (d=1.49).
Standard detection metrics inflated apparent regressions to 13.8% of scenarios due to multi-resource measurement artifacts.
36.6% of standard-mode regressions self-correct in an average of 1.2 iterations, establishing iteration 3 as the optimal stopping point for repair loops.
summary.why_it_matters: Iterative LLM repair loops require security-aware feedback mechanisms and capped iteration budgets to prevent automated code fixes from introducing silent security vulnerabilities.

security.title: InterSAGE: The Secure and Verifiable Interoperability Protocol for An Internet of Agents

summary.tldr: InterSAGE is a four-layer, trust-native protocol suite that provides persistent identity, capability-aware discovery, trust negotiation, and kernel-mediated cryptographic audit trails for inter-agent communication without requiring a consensus ledger.
key_points: Features Agent Identity Cards binding developer, code package, operator, and deployment context.
Uses DID-bound Verifiable Credential manifests for capability-aware discovery.
Combines monotonic capability attenuation with two-tier access control during trust negotiation.
Provides kernel-mediated cryptographic audit trails to bind execution and delegation traces to identity without a consensus ledger.
Complements existing communication protocols like MCP, A2A, ANP, and AG-UI as a separate trust substrate.
summary.why_it_matters: It fills a critical security gap in cross-organizational agent frameworks by establishing verifiable identity, access control, and accountability without forcing changes to underlying communication protocols.

security.title: A Hybrid LLM-Based Framework for Automated Security Annotation Generation in Business Process Models

summary.tldr: A hybrid framework combining LLMs, schema constraints, rule-based normalization, and deterministic validation automatically converts natural-language security specifications and BPMN models into valid SecBPMN2 security annotations.
key_points: Combines LLM-based semantic extraction with deterministic validation, schema-constrained mapping, and rule-based normalization.
Outperforms human security analysts in precision (0.58 vs. 0.29) while achieving similar recall (0.52 vs. 0.50) on a dataset of 27 process models.
Reduces misplaced or erroneous security annotations by nearly 50% compared to manual human analysis while accelerating generation time.
summary.why_it_matters: This hybrid automation approach enables scalable, security-by-design business process modeling by reducing manual expert effort and significantly cutting annotation errors.

security.title: CoSA: Context-Aware Severity Assessment via Context Analysis with Large Language Models

summary.tldr: CoSA automated vulnerability severity assessment by combining code property graph static pruning and agentic LLM pruning to extract repository-level context for CVSS metric prediction.
key_points: Uses a two-stage repository-pruning pipeline: lightweight static pruning on a Code Property Graph (CPG) followed by agentic LLM-guided pruning.
Consolidates pruned context into metric-wise textual summaries that feed into a lightweight transformer predictor for CVSS base metrics.
Introduces a benchmark dataset of 6,816 CVSS-labeled instances covering 90 Common Weakness Enumeration (CWE) types.
Outperforms existing baselines, achieving a 14.4% increase in prediction accuracy and a 15.3% improvement in Macro-F1 over the best baseline.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that explicit, metric-focused repository context retrieval enables reliable automated CVSS scoring, reducing the manual burden of security remediation prioritization.

security.title: STINER: Automated Extraction of Strategic Cyber Threat Intelligence from X

summary.tldr: STINER introduces a taxonomy, a 2,100-alert expert-annotated corpus, and a benchmark showing domain-adapted encoders extract strategic CTI from X more accurately and faster than fine-tuned LLMs.
key_points: Defines an eight-entity strategic CTI taxonomy focused on pivots including Threat Actor, Sector, and Location.
Benchmarked nine models across 12 configurations, including domain-adapted encoders, general-purpose baselines, open-schema extraction, and zero-shot/fine-tuned generative LLMs.
DarkBERT achieved the highest strict F1-score at 89.33%, outperforming fine-tuned LLMs while offering lower inference latency.
Applied STINER-DarkBERT to H1 2025 European threat landscape analysis, capturing early signals of the SafePay ransomware campaign before vendor retrospective reports.
summary.why_it_matters: It demonstrates that lightweight, domain-adapted encoder models can process informal social media chatter for early cyber threat detection more effectively and efficiently than large language models.

security.title: A Four-Axis Trustworthiness Benchmark for LLM-as-Judge in Principle-Based Regulation

summary.tldr: Researchers introduce Principle-Bench, a four-axis trustworthiness benchmark for LLMs evaluating principle-based regulation, alongside Ceca, a calibrated assessor providing exact per-exemplar counterfactual attributions.
key_points: Principle-Bench consists of 168 cryptoasset scenarios mapped to UK FCA principles, evaluating accuracy, paraphrase robustness, adversarial robustness, and calibration.
A 120B LLM-judge's accuracy fell from 0.74 on benign inputs to 0.27 on keyword-stuffed inputs, demonstrating severe vulnerability to adversarial 'compliance theatre'.
Inter-model agreement on keyword-stuffed inputs between two different LLM families yielded a low Cohen's kappa of 0.16, localizing failures to model architecture rather than the dataset.
Ceca (Calibrated Exemplar-Cluster Assessment) was introduced as an auditable assessor emitting exact counterfactual attributions, though no tested baseline dominated across all four axes.
summary.why_it_matters: Deploying LLM-as-a-judge systems for regulatory compliance requires measuring per-principle adversarial vulnerability and calibration, as high aggregate accuracy can mask extreme susceptibility to simple keyword manipulation.

security.title: BGA: A noise-immune neural distillation framework for malicious signature extraction in high-entropy encrypted flows

summary.tldr: The BGA framework combines ANOVA feature selection, WGAN-GP data synthesis, BiLSTM, and Adaptive Gated Multi-Head Attention to extract malicious signatures from high-entropy, encrypted TLS 1.3 flows.
key_points: ANOVA isolates high-discriminatory control-plane features and industrial setpoints from stochastic cryptographic noise.
A WGAN-GP module enforcing a 1-Lipschitz constraint addresses class imbalance across 86,878 flow records, increasing rare MSCI attack detection recall by 43.2%.
The BGA core architecture pairs BiLSTM temporal extraction with an Adaptive Gated Multi-Head Attention mechanism to filter encryption artifacts and highlight malicious signatures.
Achieves >95.2% across key metrics on CIC-IDS-2018 and Edge-IIoT benchmarks, outperforming vanilla Transformers by 8.57% under noise injection with a 0.2820 ms inference latency.
summary.why_it_matters: BGA enables accurate, low-latency detection of hidden industrial command injection attacks within heavily encrypted, high-entropy network traffic on edge gateways.

security.title: Characterizing the Variance Envelope: A Multi-Dimensional Analysis of Spectre Telemetry Across Architectures and Workloads

summary.tldr: A multi-dimensional analysis across Intel, ARM, and AMD architectures demonstrates that Spectre Hardware Performance Counter (HPC) signatures are highly fragile and easily warped by background noise, attack variants, and pacing modes.
key_points: Evaluates Spectre HPC footprints using an experimental matrix covering three attack variants, four pacing modes, and four background-noise conditions.
Analyzes the variance envelope across Intel, ARM, and AMD hardware, showing that static ML detection models fail under dynamic system noise.
Identified a persistent microarchitectural bottleneck where Prime+Probe attacks experience hardware-level failure on AMD Jaguar.
summary.why_it_matters: Reliable runtime detection of microarchitectural attacks requires adaptive, architecture-aware monitoring instead of static machine learning models.

security.title: "I Thought You Were The Uncensored Place": Norms, Rules, and Moderation in AI-Generated Sexual Content Communities

summary.tldr: An empirical interview study of 24 members and moderators from large AI-generated sexual content (AIG-SC) communities explores how anti-censorship norms and reliance on external laws complicate internal content moderation against abusive material.
key_points: Interviewed 24 members and moderators from AIG-SC communities exceeding 10,000 members that explicitly ban abusive content like AI-generated CSAM.
Identified that resources and instructions for generating sexual content are broadly accessible without user intention checks.
Found that community norms prioritizing non-judgment and anti-censorship force moderators to rely on legal limits and platform terms of service to justify moderation actions.
Exposed tensions between personal boundaries, explicit rules, and community values that create loopholes enabling abusive behavior.
summary.why_it_matters: Understanding the reliance on legal constraints over social consensus in AIG-SC communities highlights critical vulnerabilities in self-governance that technical and platform policies must address to curb abusive AI generation.

security.title: Sovereign by necessity? Frontier AI export controls, cyber security, and the limits of national AI capability

summary.tldr: Geopolitical export controls and autonomous AI cyber espionage are forcing nations to treat frontier AI access as critical cyber defence, though complete AI sovereignty remains unfeasible for most states.
key_points: In June 2026, US export restrictions required licenses for foreign access to top frontier models, causing immediate worldwide product withdrawals.
Documented cases confirm the emergence of largely autonomous, AI-run cyber espionage campaigns that alter the economics of offensive and defensive cyber operations.
Achieving true national AI sovereignty is constrained by high training costs, concentrated compute infrastructure, and limited effectiveness of state-sponsored AI programs.
A multi-layered national mitigation strategy includes inference-level sovereignty, regional capability pooling, and open-weight model hedging, which carries underappreciated political exposure.
summary.why_it_matters: States must balance national cyber resilience and AI strategy around deployment, containment, and volatile access controls rather than relying solely on full sovereign model development.

infra.title: How OneAdvanced deployed over 50 AI agents on UK-sovereign AWS

summary.tldr: OneAdvanced deployed over 50 AI agents in the UK AWS London region by self-hosting Llama 4 Maverick and Llama Guard 4 on Amazon SageMaker AI to meet strict data sovereignty requirements.
key_points: Models including Llama 4 Maverick (FP8) and Llama Guard 4 are self-hosted using vLLM on Amazon SageMaker AI using p5.48xlarge instances in the eu-west-2 region.
Orchestration uses over 50 specialized Strands agents hosted on Amazon ECS with configuration parameters stored in Amazon DynamoDB.
The RAG architecture converts documents from Amazon S3 into markdown, chunks them, and stores embeddings using the pgvector extension on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition.
Llama Guard 4 acts as a content moderation layer, evaluating user inputs for harmful content prior to main model inference.
summary.why_it_matters: Self-hosting open-weight models on dedicated cloud compute allows organizations in highly regulated sectors to deploy advanced AI agents while maintaining total in-country data sovereignty.

vendors.title: Qwen 3.8 27B is excellent, but it defaults to wildly overthinking things

summary.tldr: Alibaba released Qwen 3.8 27B, an Apache 2 licensed vision-capable LLM that features a 262,144 token context window but defaults to an over-indexing xhigh reasoning effort setting.
key_points: Qwen 3.8 27B supports adjustable reasoning_effort levels: xhigh (the default), medium, and low.
The model supports up to a 262,144 maximum context length, which prevents context exhaustion issues present at LM Studio's default 8,192 token limit.
Under the default xhigh setting, generating a complex SVG required 22,276 reasoning tokens and 21 minutes, whereas disabling reasoning took 137 seconds for 3,715 tokens.
summary.why_it_matters: Running Qwen 3.8 27B locally requires adjusting the default reasoning effort down from xhigh to prevent extreme output delays and excessive token usage on everyday tasks.

summary.tldr: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei attributes public AI skepticism to a long-standing crisis of trust in tech and institutions, arguing that real-world results like curing cancer, rather than positive marketing, are necessary to earn public confidence.
key_points: Dario Amodei rejects claims that executive risk warnings cause public anti-AI sentiment, framing it instead as a systemic trust deficit in tech and government.
Amodei dismisses glitzy marketing campaigns and positive spin, stating that claims like 'AI will cure cancer' are viewed as deceptive cliches.
Anthropic's CEO accepts the criticism that AI companies have not yet delivered on their major promises to benefit the world.
summary.why_it_matters: AI companies must deliver concrete real-world breakthroughs rather than promotional messaging to overcome public backlash and build institutional trust.

vendors.title: There are no lossless transformations of natural-language text

summary.tldr: Natural-language text rewrites by LLMs are inherently lossy because models lack the author's detailed mental representation, altering the original meaning of the text.
key_points: Every rewrite or rephrasing of natural-language text changes its underlying meaning and leads to information loss.
Engineers using LLMs to assist with writing must personally stand behind every idea and sentence in their final documents.
Attributing confusing or incorrect text to AI during code or document reviews is unacceptable, as it wastes reader time and misrepresents the author's thoughts.
summary.why_it_matters: Relying on LLMs for text transformations can unintentionally distort intent, making strict human verification essential to maintain accurate communication in technical documentation.
